propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui beatum Hermetem Martyrem tuum virtute constantiae in passione
roborasti: ex ejus nobis imitatione tribue; pro amore tuo prospera mundi
despicere, et nulla ejus adversa formidare. Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Historical source comm-s-hermetis-martyris/main/Collect/all/1; strict. Complete Latin word sequence and actual ending equal under typography only. Cross-owner reuse requires entire literal canonical Latin equality including conclusion, punctuation, wraps and final LF, SHA256 2b0c9df675310cb59fec0839b054c8f2c85d8869b47f84dda15d272a4e889443. Original target proof passage.catholic-church.missale-romanum.vatican-typica-1962.temporal-comm-s-hermetis-martyris-orations retained. No source-recipient calendar attestation or official 1962 English claimed.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: O God, Who didst strengthen blessed Hermes, Thy martyr, with the virtue of constancy in his suffering, grant us, in imitation of him, to despise the prosperity of the world for love of Thee, and not to fear worldly adversity. Through our Lord.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Sacrificium tibi, Domine, laudis offerimus in tuorum commemoratione
Sanctorum: da, quaesumus; ut, quod illis contulit gloriam, nobis prosit ad
salutem. Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n660, printed p. 652, running head `28th AUGUST`, heading `XXVIII. St. AUGUSTIN, bp. c. D.`, under which the day's commemoration is printed as `SECRET. (Of St. Hermes.)` with no Latin cue. It answers `Sacrificium tibi, Domine, laudis offerimus`. Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.

translations.text: We offer thee, O Lord, the sacrifice of praise in commemoration of thy saints: grant, therefore, we beseech thee, that what hath procured glory for them may avail to our salvation. Thro'.

propers.text:
Repleti, Domine, benedictione caelesti, quaesumus clementiam tuam: ut,
intercedente beato Hermete Martyre tuo, quae humiliter gerimus, salubriter
sentiamus. Per Dominum.

translations.text: Being fed with thy heavenly food, O Lord, we beseech thy clemency, that by the prayers of blessed Hermes, thy martyr we may partake of the salutary effects of the mysteries which we celebrate with humility. Thro'.
